Sheng Wang is a Taiwanese American stand-up comedian born on January 9, 1980, in Taipei, Taiwan. He grew up in Houston, Texas, where he attended Bellaire High School, and later earned a Bachelor of Science in Business from the University of California, Berkeley in 2002.

After graduating, Wang began performing stand-up in San Francisco and New York City, steadily building a reputation for his dry, observational style. He was a featured performer at the Montreal Comedy Festival in 2007, and in January 2011 won top honors at NBC Universal’s Seventh Annual “Stand Up for Diversity” comedy search, which included a one-year talent holding deal with the studio. That same month, Comedy Central aired his first national television special. He went on to appear on Comedy Central’s John Oliver’s New York Stand-Up Show, HBO’s 2 Dope Queens, and competed in the top ten of Last Comic Standing in 2015. From 2015 to 2018, Wang served as a staff writer and executive story editor on the ABC sitcom Fresh Off the Boat. In September 2022, he released his debut Netflix special, Sweet and Juicy, directed by Ali Wong, which received wide critical recognition.

Wang represents a generation of Taiwanese American performers who have brought their backgrounds into mainstream comedy and television. His work on Fresh Off the Boat, one of the first Asian American network sitcoms in decades, placed him at the center of a cultural moment for Asian American representation in Hollywood. The New York Times noted his approach to comedy, describing his delivery as relaxed and focused, with material that lands with precision.

Sheng Wang is a Taiwanese American stand-up comedian born on January 9, 1980, in Taipei, Taiwan. He grew up in Houston, Texas, where he attended Bellaire High School, and later earned a Bachelor of Science in Business from the University of California, Berkeley in 2002.

After graduating, Wang began performing stand-up in San Francisco and New York City, steadily building a reputation for his dry, observational style. He was a featured performer at the Montreal Comedy Festival in 2007, and in January 2011 won top honors at NBC Universal’s Seventh Annual “Stand Up for Diversity” comedy search, which included a one-year talent holding deal with the studio. That same month, Comedy Central aired his first national television special. He went on to appear on Comedy Central’s John Oliver’s New York Stand-Up Show, HBO’s 2 Dope Queens, and competed in the top ten of Last Comic Standing in 2015. From 2015 to 2018, Wang served as a staff writer and executive story editor on the ABC sitcom Fresh Off the Boat. In September 2022, he released his debut Netflix special, Sweet and Juicy, directed by Ali Wong, which received wide critical recognition.

Wang represents a generation of Taiwanese American performers who have brought their backgrounds into mainstream comedy and television. His work on Fresh Off the Boat, one of the first Asian American network sitcoms in decades, placed him at the center of a cultural moment for Asian American representation in Hollywood. The New York Times noted his approach to comedy, describing his delivery as relaxed and focused, with material that lands with precision.

 

Sheng Wang 是一位台裔美國單口喜劇演員，1980年1月9日出生於台北台灣，在德州休士頓長大，就讀於Bellaire高中，其後於2002年取得加州大學柏克萊分校商學學士學位。

畢業後，Sheng在舊金山和紐約開始投身單口喜劇表演，以其冷靜的觀察式風格逐漸建立聲譽。2007年，他受邀在蒙特婁喜劇節擔任特邀表演者；2011年1月，他在NBC環球「Stand Up for Diversity」第七屆喜劇選拔賽中奪得首獎，並獲得該電視台為期一年的人才合約。同月，喜劇中心頻道播出了他的首個全國電視特輯。此後，他陸續出現在喜劇中心的《John Oliver紐約單口喜劇秀》、HBO的《2 Dope Queens》等節目，並於2015年在《Last Comic Standing》中殺入前十強。2015年至2018年間，他在ABC情境喜劇《菜鳥新移民》中擔任編劇及執行故事編輯。2022年9月，他在Netflix發行了首部個人喜劇特輯《Sweet and Juicy》，由Ali Wong執導，廣獲好評。

Sheng Wang代表了一代將自身背景融入主流喜劇與電視的台裔美國表演者。他參與創作的《菜鳥新移民》是數十年來首批在美國主要電視網播出的亞裔美國情境喜劇之一，使他置身於亞裔美國人媒體代表性這一重要文化時刻的核心。《紐約時報》曾評價他的喜劇風格，稱其表演鬆弛而專注，笑點精準有力。
